The high catalyst / high substrate experiment has started to separate mechanisms. M18 now leads slightly, followed by M6, M8, M2. M4, M5, M14, M16, M20 are starting to fall behind. However, most mechanisms still fit within a few NLL units. I need conditions that push further separation.

Key distinctions emerging:

- M6, M8 (activation) still competitive
- M14 (catS → inactive) is losing ground
- M16 (S+catS→inactive) is losing ground
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To discriminate between the remaining mechanisms, especially M18 vs M6/M8 vs M2, I should run an experiment with LOW catalyst loading but longer time. Low catalyst will:
- Suppress M18 (2catS deactivation is bimolecular - weak at low [cat])
- Suppress M2, M3, M13 (cat dimerization)
- Suppress M19 (bimolecular in cat)
- But activation M6, M8 should show induction periods still visible
- M14 (first-order catS decay) would still deactivate at same rate
- Product inhibition effects (M12, M17) become more relevant at long times

Additionally, using a higher initial product concentration will test product inhibition mechanisms (M12, M17) more strongly.

A low catalyst + high initial product experiment will distinguish:
- M12, M17 (product inhibition) predict strong rate depression
- Mechanisms with reverse steps will show equilibrium effects
- Bimolecular cat deactivation mechanisms (M13, M18, M19) will be suppressed
</hypothesis>
